correctness.rationale: The graph Čech closed-neighborhood formula is established by the cited primary lemma. The no-triangle/no-square condition forces each horizontal-neighbor pair to have a unique generating center. Descending-cardinality pairs are actual elementary collapses; the remaining tetrahedral boundaries attach along contractible paths, yielding the integral wedge. Orientations give unsigned H2 edge permutations, signed H1 square relations, and layer-switch actions. The bundled verifier exhaustively checks 41 finite examples, including every free-face condition and independent mod-two homology; such experiments are explicitly not used as a proof of the general quantifiers.

value.rationale: This is a motivated structural classification for all connected triangle/square-free base graphs with unbounded maximum degree and cycle rank. It describes exactly how the canonical square cycles die and edge-indexed 2-sphere classes appear under intrinsic Čech thickening; integral automorphism modules distinguish more than the previously known cyclic-base Betti counts. The elementary collapses preserve simple-homotopy information and provide reproducible finite checks. This is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a mere reformulation of a known table.
